title: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral - English Studies - Intonation
exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
subject: English Studies

questions.q: What type of intonation pattern is typically used for a Yes/No question (e.g., 'Are you coming with us?')?
questions.explain: Yes/No questions usually end with a rising intonation pattern to indicate that a response is required.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Which intonation pattern is generally applied to standard statements or commands (e.g., 'Close the door.')?
questions.explain: Standard declarative sentences and definitive commands end with a falling intonation.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: A Fall-Rise (↘↗) intonation pattern is most often used to express:
options: Doubt, hesitation, or a partial agreement
questions.explain: The Fall-Rise intonation indicates that the speaker is hesitating, doubtful, or has more to add (e.g., 'She is smart, but...').
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Which intonation mark applies correctly to the command: 'Sit down immediately!'?
questions.explain: Commands and strong declarative statements naturally take a falling intonation (↘) in English.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q:
Listen/Read: 'Did you complete your homework?'
Which intonation pattern should be applied at the end of this sentence?
questions.explain: Because it is a Yes/No question, the voice generally goes up at the end, creating a rising intonation pattern (↗).
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: If a speaker responds with 'I might be able to help...', with a tone indicating hesitation and doubt, the most likely intonation pattern is:
questions.explain: A Fall-Rise intonation (↘↗) is a key indicator of hesitation, doubt, or suggesting a 'but...' implicitly.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies
